events.title: East India Company receives a royal charter
events.summary: Elizabeth I granted London merchants exclusive English trading rights east of the Cape of Good Hope.
events.limitations: Historical context does not establish institutional continuity with modern companies.

events.title: Bank of England founded
events.summary: Private subscribers financed a £1.2 million government loan, establishing the Bank of England.

events.title: Parliament regulates East India Company governance
events.summary: Parliamentary inquiries and financial difficulties produced legislation supervising the Company’s Indian administration.

events.title: Government of India Act transfers rule to the Crown
events.summary: The Act transferred governance of Company-held Indian territories to the Crown.
events.limitations: This dates a statutory transfer; it is not the Company’s dissolution date.

events.title: Federal Reserve Act signed
events.summary: President Woodrow Wilson signed the legislation establishing the Federal Reserve System.

events.title: Bretton Woods delegates design monetary institutions
events.summary: Delegates from 44 countries agreed to establish the IMF and the institution that became the World Bank.
events.limitations: Conference agreements and later legal commencement are different milestones.

events.title: Bank of England enters public ownership
events.summary: The Bank was nationalized and became wholly owned by the UK government.
events.limitations: Founding private stockholders are not evidence of present private ownership.

events.title: CIA formally established
events.summary: The National Security Act created an independent civilian foreign intelligence agency.

events.title: UN recommends partition of Mandatory Palestine
events.summary: General Assembly Resolution 181 recommended Arab and Jewish states with a special international regime for Jerusalem.
events.limitations: A recommendation is not proof of implementation or a complete account of the ensuing conflict.

events.title: U.S. leadership approves Iran covert-operation plan
events.summary: A declassified record identifies approval by the president, Secretary of State and CIA director for the campaign against Mosaddeq’s government.
events.limitations: Approval date; not the later coup date. Surviving released records are incomplete.

events.title: CIA assists overthrow of Árbenz government
events.summary: The State Department’s historical account acknowledges CIA assistance in removing Guatemala’s elected president.
events.limitations: Documents one operation, not a theory about all later Guatemalan events.

events.title: Dartmouth AI summer project proposed

events.limitations: The proposal’s appended mailing list is explicitly not a complete attendance list.

events.title: Church Committee investigates intelligence abuses
events.summary: The Senate investigated intelligence-agency misconduct and held public hearings in September and October.
events.limitations: Individual programs and agency conduct require their own records; this is not a generic “black ops” label.

events.title: Senate holds MKULTRA hearing
events.summary: CIA Director Stansfield Turner testified after additional records of the agency’s behavioral-research program were recovered.
events.limitations: Records were incomplete; the hearing does not prove claims about contemporary individuals.

events.title: BlackRock founded
events.summary: Eight founders, including Larry Fink, established the New York asset manager.
events.limitations: BlackRock and Blackwater are unrelated entities in this dataset; similar names do not establish a relationship.

events.title: NVIDIA founded

events.title: CIA establishes In-Q-Tel

coverage.scope: Selected, dated public records across historical institutions, asset management, private security, intelligence oversight, AI, conservative organizations, and specific state institutions. Not an exhaustive historical or membership database.
included: East India Company charter, parliamentary regulation and transfer of governing powers; Bank of England ownership; Federal Reserve Act; Bretton Woods; UN partition recommendation.
CIA creation, documented Iran and Guatemala interventions, Church Committee, MKULTRA hearing and CIA detention-study release.
BlackRock founding, Ukraine advisory discussions and AI infrastructure partnership; partial Blackwater/Xe–Academi–Constellis lineage; Nisur Square prosecution and pardons.
Dartmouth AI proposal, NVIDIA, In-Q-Tel, Palantir incorporation and founder governance, DeepMind, OpenAI launch supporters, Microsoft, Anthropic, AWS, MGX and GIP partnerships.
TPUSA, Charlie Kirk, Candace Owens, BLEXIT, Erika Kirk, Turning Point Action and documented PROCLAIM/BIBLEin365 professional connections.
Ukraine ministry procurement, Israeli Finance Ministry Nimbus procurement, Russian GRU indictment, Wagner sanctions, UN Ukraine resolution and ICC warrants.
limitations: Historical precedents are context, not proof of an unbroken hidden network linking every institution.
BlackRock is an asset manager, Blackwater a security-business lineage; similar names supply no evidence of affiliation.
Constellis acquired selected predecessor businesses, not all Blackwater assets or intellectual property. Its account says Erik Prince does not own Constellis.
Country labels must not imply collective guilt; the graph uses ministries, agencies, governments and named individuals.
Contracts, funding, attendance, employment and advisory roles are distinct. A connection is not evidence of conspiracy or complicity.
No claim is made that Erika Kirk or TPUSA has an intelligence or criminal affiliation. Unsupported assassination and trafficking rumors were excluded.
No complete roster of covert personnel or “all AI companies” is claimed; public records cannot establish that scope.
Official organizational pages establish announced roles and transactions, not independent verification of self-promotional performance claims.
Arrest warrants, indictments and sanctions are labeled separately from convictions. Records describe historical actions, not necessarily current case status.
The IQT–Palantir investment is widely reported but was not included as a dated edge because this pass did not locate a primary source establishing date and terms.
No claimed Palantir–Israeli Defense Ministry operational edge was added from a company media index; the Nimbus procurement edges use direct government/vendor records.
Events with year or month precision are not assigned invented days; access-date relationships are explicitly marked as observations.
